references.text: The Lord sent poisonous snakes among the people, and they bit the Israelites so that many died. This describes the same event with the seraph serpents in the wilderness.
Moses struck the rock at Horeb, and water came out of it. This is the event where God gave water from the rock in the wilderness.
Moses struck the rock, and plenty of water came out. This is another account of water from the rock in the wilderness.
He split rocks in the wilderness and gave them abundant drink as from the great deep. He made streams flow out of the mountain. This refers to the same miracle of water from the rock.
He opened the rock, and water flowed out. It ran like a river through the dry land. This describes the same wonder of water from the rock.
He who turned the rock into a pool, the hard stone into a spring of water. This refers to the miracle of water from the rock.
They did not thirst when he led them through the wasteland. He made water flow out of the rock for them. He split the rock, and water flowed.
All drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ. Paul interprets the water from the rock typologically.
The Lord led the people through the wilderness, a land of wasteland and ravines, a land of drought and shadow of death. This describes the great and terrible wilderness.
